translations.text: The conversion of King Mirian, and with him of all Kartli, by our holy and blessed mother Nino the apostle. First let us recall the life of the holy and
blessed one, our mother and the enlightener of all Kartli, Nino the apostle, which that blessed one herself told us at the time of her death,
and which the believing queen Salome of Ujarma wrote down. She was the wife of King Mirian's son and the daughter of Tiridates, king of the Armenians.
In those times, when Saint George of Cappadocia was martyred for Christ, there was a certain man from a city of Cappadocia,
a servant of God fit to be among the princes, named Zabilon. He went to Rome, before the emperor, to serve him and to receive rewards from him.
In those same days there was a certain man in Kolastra who had two children, a son and a daughter. His son's name was Juvenal and his daughter's was Susanna.
The husband and wife died, and the brother and sister were left orphans. They rose up and went to the holy city of Jerusalem.
They set their hope on the holy Resurrection, the hope of all Christians, and devoted themselves to it there.
There this brother, Juvenal, obtained the office of [?], while his sister Susanna served Sara Niaphor of Bethlehem.
Meanwhile this Cappadocian youth named Zabilon, whom we mentioned, reached Rome and came before the emperor.
At that time the Branjs [Franks] had risen up to make war on the Romans, on the plain of Patalan.
The Lord gave invincible strength to Zabilon, that Cappadocian youth, and he stood against enemies beyond number.
He routed the Branjs, captured the king of the Branjs and all his princes, and brought them before the emperor.
The emperor sentenced them to death. Then the Branjs began to weep, and they begged Zabilon:
"First give us your faith and bring us into the temple of your God, and only then let our death come.
For you yourself captured us, so you yourself do this for us, and you will be innocent of our blood, O valiant one."
When Zabilon heard this, he quickly told their words to the emperor and the patriarch. They baptized them, with Zabilon as their sponsor.
They brought them into the temple of God, gave them communion in the holy mysteries, the body and blood of Christ, and showed them the glories of the apostles.
Early in the morning those Franks got up and put on burial clothes,
and went out to the place where people were slaughtered and blood was shed. They prayed and thanked God for baptism, and said:
"In death we are immortal, for God has made us worthy to receive such glory
the provision that never runs out, the body and blood of Christ, the immortal Son of God, who is higher than all mountains and deeper than all abysses, and who is blessed forever.
But woe to our offspring, the fruits of bitterness and the heirs of darkness." And they cried out: "Let the swordsman come and take our heads from us."
When Zabilon saw this, he was moved in his mind and wept bitterly. For like sheep they bowed their heads to be cut off,
and gave themselves up to death, and like lambs they mourned pitifully for their children.
Then Zabilon, filled with pity for them, went before the emperor and begged from him the men who had been made ready for death. The emperor granted them to him and said:
"I have granted them to you; do with them whatever you wish." And he let them go.
But they begged Zabilon to go with them to their country and give the law of Christ, baptism by water, to all their people.
He heard their plea, asked the patriarch for a priest, and received an order from the king. And they set off joyfully.
When they were one day's journey away, news went ahead of them: "The king is alive, and he is coming, and all the princes are with him."
Then the ten principalities set out: Khozama, Khoza, Gaakhilaja, Tenebaga, Khingaragi, Zija, Zaga,
Zada, Zarma, and the royal Tmonidi. All of these came to meet them at a great, deep river.
The king divided the people and placed them on both sides of the water. The priests blessed the water, and all the people went down into it.
They washed and came up at a single landing place [or: on the east side], and Zabilon laid his hand on all the people. He stayed there ten days.
He gave all those people communion in the mystery of Christ, left priests with them, and set up for them the whole order of the Christian faith.
After this he parted from them, bade them all farewell in peace, and left with great gifts for Rome. And he resolved in his mind:
"I will go to Jerusalem and devote these gifts of mine to the service of God's holy places."
He went to Jerusalem, and when he reached Jerusalem he distributed all his possessions to the poor, according to God's commandment.
And he saw that the devtalari [?] mentioned earlier had become patriarch. Zabilon and the patriarch became close friends.
Then Sarah Niaphor spoke to the patriarch in this way: "This Zabilon, father and baptizer of the Franks, is a man perfect in fear of God and in wisdom in every way.
So give him your sister Susanna as his wife." Then the holy patriarch was pleased with
this proposal of Sarah Niaphor, and he gave Susanna to Zabilon as his wife. And Zabilon went to his own city, Kolastra.
Saint Nino, the teacher of Kartli, was born of them, their only child, with no other children. Her mother Susanna raised her in the service of the poor.
When Nino was twelve years old, her parents sold everything they had, went to Jerusalem, and distributed it to the poor.
When they reached Jerusalem, Zabilon received the sign of the cross from the patriarch and separated from his wife.
He pressed his daughter, this holy Nino, to his breast, poured tears from his eyes onto her face like springs of water, and said to her:
"My only daughter, now I am leaving you an orphan, without me, and I entrust you to your Father in heaven and to God who nurtures all.
For he is the father of orphans and the judge of widows. Do not be afraid, my child. Take up the zeal of Mary Magdalene and of Lazarus's sisters for the love of Christ.
If you love him as they loved him, he will likewise give you everything you ask of him."
When he had said this, he gave her the kiss of eternal farewell and went beyond the Jordan to the wild people. Where he lived is known only to God, the all-knowing Creator.
The patriarch appointed the mother of holy Nino to serve poor and sick women.
And Saint Nino served Niaphora, an Armenian woman of Dvin, for two years, and she asked her about all the sufferings of Christ:
about his crucifixion, burial and resurrection, and about his garment, the linen cloths and the shroud, and the cross, and she inquired into everything else, one thing after another,
for there had never been anyone, and there was no one in Jerusalem, equal to her in knowledge of the law, both the Old and the New, thorough in every respect.
And she began to teach her, and said: "My child, I see that your strength is like the strength of a lioness,
who roars over all the four-footed beasts, or like a female eagle, who rises higher into the air than the male,
and takes in all the dry land within the pupil of her eye, as though it were the size of a small pearl. She surveys and searches out her food like fire.
And when she sees it, she folds her wings and swoops down on it. In the same way your life will be guided by the Holy Spirit.
Now I will begin and tell you everything. When mortal men saw the immortal God on earth, who had come to call the gentiles,
since he himself willed the salvation of the world, he began to do good to the Jews: raising the dead, giving sight to the blind and healing the sick.
They grew jealous of this and plotted together, and they sent soldiers throughout the whole land to summon the Jews to come quickly,
and they said: "Look, we are perishing. Come, all of you, and gather together."
Then countless men came from every land, learned in the law of Moses, who opposed the Holy Spirit. And they carried out whatever was destined to be done to Christ:
they crucified him and cast lots for his garment, and by that lot it fell to the northerners, the citizens of Mtskheta.
And when those Jews buried Christ, they laid him in the tomb and sealed his tomb.
But he rose, as he had said beforehand, and the linen cloths were found in the tomb.
When dawn came, all this was made known. And Pilate came, and Pilate's wife too, to the tomb of Christ.
And when the linen cloths were found, Pilate's wife took them and went quickly to Pontus, to her home, and became a believer in Christ.
Some time later, they came into the hands of Luke the Evangelist, and he put them away in a place that he himself knows.
But the shroud was not found, although some people said about Peter:
"He was able to take [?] it, and he had it." But they did not tell us this openly, as they did the other things.
The crosses are buried in this same city of Jerusalem, but no one knows where they are;
when God wills it, they too will come to light." When Saint Nino had heard all this from Sara
Niaphora, she gave thanks to God and blessed him. And she asked her again: "Where in the north is
that land to which the lot fell for those Jews who had come, and where they carried off the garment of our Lord Jesus Christ?" Sara Niaphora answered her and said:
"In the east there is a city called Mtskheta, in the land of Kartli and Armenia. It is a pagan mountain country, but at this time it has been made a dominion of the Uzhiks [?]."
And in those days a certain woman came from Ephesus to venerate the Holy Resurrection, and Sara Niaphora asked that woman:
"Is Queen Helena also in the same error and darkness?" And she answered her thus:
"I am their handmaid, and I know all their intentions, open and hidden. And I know this about her: she has a great longing for the faith of Christ and for baptism."
When holy Nino heard this from that woman, she said to Niaphor:
"Send me, and let me go before Queen Helena. Perhaps I may come into her presence to speak for Christ."
And Niaphor told the patriarch of this desire and of Nino's purpose.
Then her mother's brother called holy Nino, his sister's daughter, and stood her on the step of the holy altar.
He laid his holy hands on her shoulders, sighed toward heaven from the depths of his heart, and said: "O Lord, God of the ages, into your hands I commit
this orphan child of my sister, and I send her out to preach your Godhead, so that she may proclaim the good news of your resurrection.
Wherever her course is pleasing to you, O Christ God, be her fellow traveller, her harbour, her teacher, and her interpreter of languages, as you were to those of old who feared your name."
And she took leave of her mother with a parting kiss, and he made the sign of the cross over her. And so, with prayer to God and with a blessing, he sent her away.
Holy Nino set out with the woman who had come from Ephesus. When they reached the royal city of Rome, at the house of the woman
with whom she had travelled, they found a certain princess of royal lineage named Rhipsime, and her nurse Gaiane,
in a convent of virgins. Because they confessed Christ, they longed for baptism and were waiting to receive it from Jerusalem.
Then the woman brought holy Nino, handed her over to holy Rhipsime, and told her Nino's story. When Rhipsime, the lover of Christ, saw her,
she embraced her with joy and received holy Nino into her own house and into her company, from the hands of the woman who had travelled with her.
While holy Nino was staying with her, in that same year Rhipsime received the baptism she had longed for,
and with her Gaiane her nurse and others of her household, fifty more souls in number.
Most of them were baptized at the hands of holy Nino. Then they all went to their convent, and holy Nino stayed with them for two years.
In those days the emperor sent men to search for a comely and beautiful girl, so that they might find him one worthy to be his wife.
When the searchers reached that convent of virgins, they saw Rhipsime. They studied her appearance and asked about her lineage, for no one was like Rhipsime in looks.
They painted her likeness on a board and sent it to the emperor. The emperor was pleased and filled with joy, and he ordered the wedding to be celebrated
with great rejoicing. For this purpose he quickly sent messengers and officials throughout all his dominions,
so that everyone would gather with gifts and come with great joy at the king's command to the royal wedding.
But when those all-holy women saw the enemy's hidden scheme and his fiery arrows,
with which he was rushing to pierce the holy virgins, they were grieved. For the king had become a vessel of wrath, like the serpent that became the instrument of ruin [?] in paradise,
In the same way, here too, like him, was this lawless one, who held to the defiled worship of foul and abominable idols.
When the blessed Rhipsime, Gaiane and the other holy and all-praised women saw that this trial had come upon them, they remembered
the spotless vow and the praiseworthy solitary life in which they had been trained,
and they wept and lamented over the portrait that had been painted and sent to the lawless king to show him the beauty of holy Rhipsime.
They prayed without ceasing and bound themselves to the strictest rules, beseeching the all-merciful God with many supplications.
And by a common resolve among themselves, all fifty-three souls secretly left that land.
They came as fugitives to the regions of Armenia, to the place called the New City, built by Valarsh [?], which is Dvin, the residence of the king of the Armenians.
There they went into the winepresses of a vineyard that stood on the north and east side, and there they supported themselves by trading the work of their hands.
The emperor was filled with grief, and he sent men to every place to search for them.
Then the emperor's envoys came before Tiridates, king of the Armenians, and delivered to him the emperor's letter, in which it was written as follows:
"The autocrat emperor greets my beloved brother, friend and fellow ruler Tiridates.
Let your brotherhood and alliance be informed of all that has befallen us from that misguided race of the Christians.
For our authority is utterly despised by their community, and
our sovereignty is scorned by them. For they serve some crucified dead man, worship wood, and honor the bones of men,
and they count their own death for the sake of their lord as glory. They do not fear [?] from the Jews, yet they fear the one crucified by the Jews, and they are deluded.
They even revile kings and despise the gods. They count as nothing the power of the light of the sun, moon and stars, and say instead that these were created by that crucified one.
In this way they have turned the land upside down, so that husbands have separated from their wives and wives from their husbands while still alive.
Although we have destroyed them with great threats and severe tortures, they have multiplied all the more.
Now it happened that I saw a young maiden of their race, and I resolved to take her as my wife.
But her heart did not desire me as is fitting toward a king; instead they regarded me as hateful and impure.
For this reason they have fled secretly from me and have gone to the regions of your land.
Be it known to you, my brother: seek them out, and when you find her companions, put them to death.
But the one whom they led astray, beautiful in appearance and named Rhipsime, send to me.
And if she pleases you, desire her for yourself, for no other like her has been found in the land of the Greeks. And live well in the service of the gods."
As soon as Tiridates had read this command of the emperor, he immediately began to search for them, and he found them in the winepresses mentioned before.
And when he saw Rhipsime, he was filled with desire and rejoiced with great joy, and he resolved to take her as his wife. But holy Rhipsime would not submit to him.
Then he martyred her, her nurse Gaiane, and many others who were with them, as their martyrdom and the miracle are written in the Conversion of the Armenians.
For by the judgment of God, King Tiridates was turned into a boar. But some of those saints hid and fled.
Then this holy Nino hid among the thorns of a rose bush, which was not yet in bloom at that time.
And as the souls of those holy martyrs were going up, holy Nino saw a deacon like Stephen coming down, wearing a stole of light;
and in his hands he held a censer, from which came fragrant smoke that covered the heavens, and with him was a multitude of the heavenly hosts.
And the souls of the holy martyrs joined them. When holy Nino saw this, she cried out:
"Lord, Lord, why do you leave me among asps and vipers?" Then she heard a voice from above,
which said to her: "So shall your taking-up be too, when this thorn bush around you has all turned into fragrant rose petals.
Arise and go northward, where the harvest is great and there are no labourers."
And holy Nino set out from there and came to Orbani, on the borders of Armenia, and she spent the winter there in many hardships.
And in the fourth month, which is June, she set out and reached the mountains of Javakheti, where she came upon a great lake with a river flowing out of it, which is called Paravani.
And when she looked out from there, she saw the northern mountains; for even in those summer days they were full of snow and bitter air.
And holy Nino trembled and said: "Lord, Lord, take my soul from me."
And she stayed there two days, and asked the fishermen who fished in that lake for food.
And there were also shepherds in that same place, and they were keeping the night watch [?] over their flock;
and they called on their gods Armaz and Zaden, and vowed offerings to them, saying: "when we return in peace."
Now holy Nino knew a little Armenian, for she had learned it earlier from Niaphori, and she found among those shepherds one who spoke Armenian and asked him:
"What country are you from?" And he answered her and said: "We are from the villages of Elarbini and Sapurtsli, and from Kindzara; we live in the suburbs of the great
city of Mtskheta, where the gods are worshipped as gods and the kings reign as kings." And she asked, "Where is Mtskheta?"
And the shepherd told her only this: that the river flowing out of this lake goes to Mtskheta.
And holy Nino laid down a stone as a pillow, lay down, and fell asleep at the outflow of that lake.
And while she was asleep, a man came to her in a vision. He was of medium height, and his hair was half-length [?]. He gave a sealed letter to Saint Nino and said:
"Take this to Mtskheta, to the king of the heathens." But Saint Nino began to weep and plead with him:
"Lord, I am a foreign and ignorant woman, and I do not even know the language. How can I go to a foreign land and among foreign peoples?"
Then the man unrolled that book and gave it to her to read. It was written in Latin, and it bore the seal of Jesus.
Ten sayings were written in that book. 1. Wherever this gospel is preached, there this woman too shall be spoken of.
2. There is neither male nor female, but you are all one.
3. Go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son,
and of the Holy Spirit. 4. A light has shone out upon the Gentiles, for the glory of your people Israel.
5. Wherever this gospel of the kingdom is preached, there it shall be spoken of throughout the whole world.
6. Whoever hears you and receives you has received me; and whoever receives me shall receive the one who sent me.
7. For Mary loved the Lord greatly, because she always listened to his word of truth.
8. Do not be afraid of those who kill your bodies but cannot kill the soul. 9. Jesus said to Mary Magdalene:
"Go, woman, and bring the good news to my sisters and brothers." 10. Wherever you preach in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
When Saint Nino had read these sayings, she began to pray to God, and she understood that the vision had come from heaven.
She lifted her eyes to heaven and asked for his help [?from the next day on].
After this she set out toward the river of the lake, which flowed toward the west.
She travelled hard and rough roads. She met great hardships on the way and great terror from wild beasts, until she reached the place where the water began to flow toward the east.
From then on she found comfort, because she met travellers there. With them she reached the region of Kartli, at the city called Urbnisi,
where she saw a people of foreign races who served gods, for they worshipped fire, stones and wood as god. Because of this the soul of this saint was grieved,
and she went into the synagogue of the Jews for the sake of the Hebrew language. She stayed there one month and studied the character of this land.
Then one day great crowds set out from that city, going to Mtskheta, the great royal city, to trade some goods and to sacrifice before Armaz, their god.
The saint went along with them. When they reached the city of Mtskheta, they stopped on the far side, at the bridge of the Magi.
Saint Nino saw the magic and error of those fire-worshipping peoples. Saint Nino wept over their perdition and mourned her own life as a stranger in a foreign land.
And behold, on the next day there was a sound of [?] and of trumpets. Countless people came out, like the flowers of the field, and a terrifying din went up, though the king had not yet come out.
When the time came, everyone began to flee and hide in every direction. Each person fled in fear to his own shelter.
And behold, Queen Nana suddenly came out, and the people came slowly. They decorated all the streets with garments of every colour and with leaves.
All the people began to praise the king. Then King Mirian came out, terrifying in appearance, too dazzling for the eye to look at.
Saint Nino asked a certain Jewish woman, "What is this?" And she said to her:
"They declare [?] him Armazi, the god of gods, and there is no other idol besides him." Then Saint Nino immediately went to see Armazi.
And those mountains were filled with banners and people, as fields are filled with flowers.
And Saint Nino reached the fortress of Armazi and stood near that idol, in a cleft of the wall.
And she saw a marvel that passed understanding and could not be put into words: the terrifying, soul-shaking fear of the kings, the princes and all the people standing before those idols.
And Saint Nino saw that there stood a man of copper. His body was clothed in a coat of golden mail, and on his head was a strong helmet.
His eyes were set with emerald and beryl. In his hands he held a sword that shone like lightning and turned about in his hands.
If anyone touched it, he gave himself up to death, and people would say:
"Woe is me! Perhaps I have fallen short in honouring this great god Armazi, or perhaps we have entered into talk with the Hebrews, or with the magi, in listening [?];
and because of what strangers say about some foreign god, may he not find some fault in me and strike me with that sword of his, which everyone fears."
And they worship it in fear. And again, on its right was a man of gold, and his name was Gatsi; and
on its left stood a man of silver, and his name was Gaim. These were thought to be gods by the people of Kartli.
Then blessed Nino wept and sighed to God for the errors of the people of the northern land: the light was hidden from them, and darkness ruled over them.
For she looked at those mighty kings and all the princes, who had been swallowed alive into hell. They had abandoned the Creator
and worshipped stones and wood, copper and wrought brass as god, and they held these to be the maker of all things.
Then she remembered the word that the patriarch Juvenal, the holy father, had commanded her:
"I send you out as a mature man, and you will reach a foreign land and the peoples darageveli zepel bakadul [?], which in the Frankish language is:
"men who have fallen away from God." Then she lifted her eyes to heaven and said:
"Lord, through the greatness of your power your enemies have lied to you, and through your great long-suffering you bear [?] what these enemies do and plot on the earth.
But do not disregard them, for man is your image. For man's sake one of the Holy Trinity became man and saved the whole world.
Look with mercy on these peoples too. Rebuke these disobedient spirits, the rulers of the world and princes of darkness, and cast them down into hard places.
And show me, O Lord, God of my father and my mother, to this handmaid

of yours and their offspring, so that all the ends of the earth may see your salvation, so that the north may rejoice together with the south, and so that every tongue may worship you, the only God, through Christ Jesus,
your Son, to whom thanksgiving and the proclaiming of glory are due."
And when Saint Nino had finished this prayer, in no more than the blink of an eye, winds and gales rose from the west
and roared with thunder, with a terrifying sound, and clouds quickly appeared with a dreadful sign.
And the breeze from the west brought a smell of bitter [?] (jerkuli) and of foul gall.
When the crowd of people saw it coming upon them, every man fled to the city and to the villages.
Time was given until the people had reached their homes.
And at once that cloud of wrath arrived, bitterly fierce, and it brought down hailstones each the weight of a litra, on that place alone, the dwelling of the idols.
It ground the idols into small pieces and smashed them. The fierce wind tore down the walls and scattered them into the clefts of the rocks.
But holy Nino stayed safe and in peace in the place where she had first gone in.
On the second day King Mirian and all the people came out. They searched for their gods and did not find them.
Because of this, fear and trembling fell upon them. That hard-hearted people mourned and said: "The god of the Chaldeans,
Itrujan, and this god of ours, Armaz, are complete enemies. This one once turned the sea against him, and now he has taken his revenge, and it is by him that this has come."
But others said: "The God by whose power King Tiridates was turned into a boar, and by the power of the same God was made a man again, that God is the one who has brought this about.
For no other god is able to do such a thing."
They said this because King Tiridates had been turned into a boar by the power of Christ, and by the power of Christ had been turned back into a man.
From then on the praise and glory of Christ was no longer spoken in secret in Kartli, for the grace of God had begun to spread over the East.
On that same day of wrath, when the hail and the fierce wind had died down, holy Nino came out of the cleft in the rock and found that beryl gem.
She picked it up and went forward toward the end of the rock of the cave, where an old fortress had once stood. There stood a single [?] (brinji) tree,
beautiful, tall and with many branches, where King Bartam had had his shady spot and resting place.
She went under that tree, marked out the sign of the cross of Christ, and prayed there for six days.
She gave thanks to God and begged him to look with mercy on that misled people and to free them from the devil.
When this happened it was the sixth hour, on the sixth day of the month in which Emmanuel, on Tabor, showed the image of the Father to the chief of the disciples and the chief of the prophets.
Then a lady of the royal court named Shroshana came and saw her under the tree. She was amazed and brought a woman who spoke Greek, and asked Nino about her journey.
Holy Nino told her all about her journey and her affairs, except that she said nothing about her mother and her brothers, for she spoke of herself as a captive.
Then Shroshana took pity on her because she was a stranger. Her eyes filled with tears, and she pressed Nino to go with her to the royal house.
But holy Nino did not want to go with her, and Shroshana went away.
On the third day after this, Nino came down to Kartli, crossed the Mtkvari, and made her way to the king's garden,
where the pillar raised up by God and the catholicos's church now stand. When she came to the gate of the garden, she saw the small house of the garden's keeper.
Saint Nino went in, and a woman named Anasto was sitting inside.

When the woman saw her, she stood up, pleaded with her and welcomed her warmly, as if she knew her. She washed her hands, anointed her with oil, and brought her bread and wine. Saint Nino stayed with her for nine months.
Now this Anasto and her husband had no children, and they grieved greatly because they were childless.
Then Saint Nino saw a vision. A man the colour of light came and said to her: "Go into that garden. There is a [?] (babilo) under the small fir trees,
mixed with [?] of the Lord. Take earth from that place and give it to those people to eat, and a child will be granted to them." Saint Nino did this and said to them:
"By the power of Christ, the Son of God, who has no beginning, who shares the throne with the Father and the Holy Spirit, who became man for our salvation, was crucified,

was buried, and rose on the third day, who ascended into heaven and sat down at the right hand of the Father, and who will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead: may he give you understanding."
And she taught them the whole true way. Then the husband and wife confessed Christ and secretly became disciples.
Then outside the city walls Saint Nino found a bush, a blackberry bramble, where the altar of the upper episcopal church now stands, and she made it her dwelling.
She made a cross from vine cuttings and set it up under that bush, and she prayed there constantly, day and night, without stopping.
The husband and wife served her, and they marvelled at her ascetic labours: her fasting, her prayer and her keeping watch through the night.
She often went to the Jewish quarter to learn the Hebrew language and to search for the tunic of the Lord. She had heard in Jerusalem from Niaphor that
"the Jews of Mtskheta took away the tunic of the Lord." For this reason she asked questions among those Jews, so that she might learn something about the tunic.
She found a Jewish priest named Abiathar, and she preached the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ to him and to his daughter Sidonia.
They believed and became disciples, they and six other Jewish women.
They took up the yoke of Saint Nino's teaching without being baptised, because no priest could be found to baptise them, and they were her disciples in secret.
By the power of Christ she performed healings and wonders. She healed many who were paralysed, [?] by means of medicine.
She lived this way in the city of Mtskheta for three years in all. During that time King Mirian and his brother's son, the great king of the Persians, made an expedition
into Greek territory, when Constantine, king of the Greeks, by the power of Christ and with the cross leading the way, drove off the kings and slaughtered their countless armies.

The account of Abiathar the priest, who became a disciple of the holy and blessed Nino. I, Abiathar the priest, was the one chosen by lot to serve in the year when this holy and blessed Nino came to Mtskheta.
At that same time a letter reached me from Antioch, from the priests of the Jews. In it was written:
"God has split the kingdom of Israel into three. Look, our prophets have fallen silent, and everything the Spirit moved them to speak has been fulfilled, and we have been scattered
over all the earth, and the Romans have seized our land. We weep together with our people, because we have angered God the Creator.
Now examine the books of Moses and the word that he wrote for us, all of this, namely:
"the one who said on earth that he himself was the Son of God, they put him to death." Or perhaps, then, we have gone astray over the death of Jesus the Nazarene.
For we see that whenever our forefathers sinned against God and forgot him altogether, he would hand them over to a harsh power and to captivity;
and whenever they turned back and cried out, he would quickly deliver them from their affliction. "This we know from Scripture to have happened seven times.
But now, since those fathers of ours laid hands on that son of the poor stranger woman and killed him,
God has withdrawn the hand of his mercy from us. He has shattered our kingdom, removed us from his holy temple, and utterly disregarded our people.
And it has been three hundred years and more since that time that he has not heard our prayer, nor has he given us any relief.
For this reason it seems likely to us that perhaps such a dispensation was indeed from heaven." The writing has grown long.
And when I heard this, I began to ask that woman Nino about Christ: who he was, and for what reason the Son of God became man.
Then holy Nino opened her mouth like a gushing spring and began
to speak from the beginning of the ages. She recited our books from memory and explained them to me. She roused me as if I were asleep, and brought me to understanding as if I had been senseless,
and she made me pity our fathers, and convinced me of the change of the law, until I believed her words:
Jesus Christ, the Son of God; his passion and resurrection; his fearful second coming; and that he is the one in whom the expectation of the Gentiles lies.
My child and I were made worthy to receive that sprinkling which purifies from sins, the water of the baptismal font, which David longed for and could not attain.
And I heard the sound of the new law, ah, of the hymns which David longed for.
And we were made worthy to partake of the body and blood of Christ the Son of God, the Lamb offered for the sins of the world, whose taste is sweet.
And after this, O Lord, grant my departure from my body.
And again, my eyes saw many miracles in Mtskheta, performed by holy Nino in our days."
The account of the same priest Abiathar concerning the tunic of our Lord Jesus Christ: "I, Abiathar, relate to you the account
which was made known to me, which I heard with my own ears from my father and mother, and which I also know from books. For
they too had been told it this way, through the stories and by the hearing of their own grandfathers and parents:
When Herod was reigning in Jerusalem, word reached us that "the Persians have captured Jerusalem."
Because of this there was mourning and grief among the Jews of Kartli: the inhabitants of Mtskheta, the priests of Bodi,
the scribes of Kodis-Tsqaro, and the Canaanite interpreters of Sobi. All of these were moved to flee.
But after a few days a message of comfort arrived:
"The Persians did not come to capture Jerusalem. Instead of weapons they carried royal gold, myrrh that heals wounds quickly, and sweet-smelling incense.
And they were seeking a certain child who had been born, a son of David, and behold, they found a stranger, born of a stranger woman, out of due time and in a place that was no place.
And they came to worship that child, and offered him the gifts. And there was great joy among all the Jews of Kartli.
"But after this, when thirty years had passed, Annas the priest wrote from Jerusalem to my grandfather (my father's father) Elioz, saying:
'He for whose sake the Persian kings came with gifts has grown up and has reached the full measure
of maturity, and he calls himself the Son of God. Come, all of you, to his death, so that the commandment of Moses may be fulfilled.'
And Elioz, my grandfather, an old man, went from here. He had a mother from the tribe of Eli the priest, and he had one sister.
And his mother pleaded with Elioz, saying: 'Go, my son, at the summons of the king and according to the rule of the law;
but do not let your mind take part in what they are plotting, no, my son, for he is the word of the prophets and the parable of the wise.'
And Elioz of Mtskheta and Longinus of Karsani went, and they arrived there in time for the crucifixion of the Lord.
And when they nailed the Lord, and the executioner struck the nails with the hammer, Elioz's mother heard it here, and she shrieked and said:
'Farewell, kingdom of the Jews, for you have killed your own Savior and have become the murderers of the Creator.
Woe is me, that I did not die before this, so that my ears would not have heard it.' And with this she died.

"And the tunic of the Lord fell by lot to the people of Mtskheta. Elioz took it and brought it to Mtskheta. And his sister came to meet him, drenched in tears. She threw her arms around her brother's neck
and took the garment of Jesus from him, pressed it to her breast, and at once her spirit departed, because of these three griefs:
for the death of Christ, for her mother, and for her brother, who had taken part in the blood of the Lord.
"Then there was great wonder and agitation in Mtskheta, for the great King Aderki himself was amazed, and so was the whole multitude of the people and the princes.

And King Aderki desired that garment. But that wonder struck him with terror and fear, and he would not take it from the hands of the dead woman, who held it clasped to her breast firmly and with longing.
And Elioz buried his sister with the garment of the Lord still in her hands. And that place is one that only the Lord knows.
Many years later, King Armazael, the great-grandson of King Aderki, searched among the Jews for that garment and did not find it.
For they told him everything that had happened, but no one knew the place, except for this:
that 'it is near the cedar that was brought from Lebanon and planted in Mtskheta and grew there.'
For our mother, holy Nino, many times ordered us to search for that garment, but she too had told us only this much:
'It is a place over which the tongues of men will never fall silent in singing to God.'
And the house of Elioz was in the west of the city, beyond Moguta, at the bridge.
In those days holy Nino many times saw a vision in her short sleep upon her knees: behold, birds of the sky came, black in color,
And they would go down into the river, wash themselves and become pure white, and go up into the garden, and they would [?] the buds and feed on the flowers,
and so lovingly and eagerly they would come to Saint Nino, since the garden was hers, and would gather around her, chirping beautifully.
Saint Nino told this to her disciple Sidonia, daughter of Abiathar. And Sidonia said to Saint Nino:
"O stranger, captive born here, and deliverer of captives, know that through you this new time has come, and because of you that old story is heard:
what our fathers did to that heavenly man, the unjust shedding of that innocent blood, through which shame came upon the Jews:
scattering to the ends of heaven, fall from kingship, the taking away of that holy temple, the calling of a foreign people, and the giving of their glory to them. Jerusalem, Jerusalem,
how you have spread out your wings and gather all the nations from the ends of heaven under your wings.
Behold, here too this woman has come, who will change every custom of this land." And she turned again to Saint Nino and said:
"This vision is about you, for this place will become a paradise through you."
"Now when King Mirian came from Greece, driven away by King Constantine, Saint Nino's preaching of the faith of Christ had already been made public before his coming.
For she said in a loud voice: "I have found the inhabitants of the north in error," and she showed that cross of vine, and with it she worked great wonders.
For she healed the paralyzed without medicine, by the touch of the cross.
And her disciples preached with her, those who had earlier become her disciples in secret: seven women of Jewish descent, Sidonia, daughter of Abiathar, and six others;
and the married couple who kept the garden, and Abiathar the priest, that new Paul, who preached the faith of Christ fearlessly and tirelessly,
who was very learned in the old law, had learned this new law from Saint Nino, and convinced everyone of the true faith even more than Nino did.
Then the Jews rose up against Abiathar to stone him.
But King Mirian sent servants and rescued Abiathar from death, for King Mirian had a desire for the faith of Christ. For he had heard of the miracle
of the faith of Christ from Greece and Armenia, and he did not stop Nino and her disciples from preaching.
But the devil, that invisible enemy, fought against him, and he could not stand firm in confessing Christ.
And Queen Nana was exceedingly hard-hearted and scorned that preaching.
And Saint Nino prayed unceasingly in her shelter under the brambles.
And the pagans were amazed at her prayer and her vigils, and the matter seemed strange to them;
they began to question her, and she taught them the Old and New books, made those foolish and undiscerning people wise, and planted love of Christ in their hearts.
And so it went for three years from the time she made the preaching of Christ public, and she made many disciples.
At that time there was a certain little child with a grievous illness, and his mother carried him around from door to door, hoping to find someone skilled in healing who might help him.
And all of them examined him, but they never found anything that would help to heal the child.
And the physicians told the woman: "Nothing can help that child."
Now that woman was a pagan and hard-hearted. She always despised the faith of the Christians, and she also kept others from going to Saint Nino and seeking her out.
When the physicians had left her without hope, she came and fell down before Saint Nino and begged her to heal the child. Then Saint Nino said:
"I do not practise the kind of healing that comes from men. But my God, Christ, will give healing to that child, whom everyone has given up for lost
as lost." And Saint Nino ordered the child to be laid on the haircloth on which she always prayed, and she began to pray to God.
At that very moment the child was healed, and she gave him back alive to his mother. The child's mother confessed Christ and said:
"There is no other God except Christ, whom Nino preaches." She became a disciple of Saint Nino, followed in her footsteps, and glorified God.
Then Queen Nana fell into a great and bitter illness, which no one was able to cure.
For all the skilled physicians used up all their medicines and could not cure her. They were at a loss and gave up hope.
But some people told the queen: "Through the prayer of that woman, the Roman captive whose name is Nino, many sick people are healed."
Then she ordered her servants to bring Nino to her.
The queen's servants went and found Saint Nino in the hut under the bramble bush, praying at the sixth hour, and they told her the queen's order. But Saint Nino said:
"I have not been commanded to go out to where our comfort is not. Instead, let the queen come to this dwelling of mine, and she will truly be healed by the power of Christ."
The servants reported Nino's words to the queen. Then the queen earnestly said to them:
"Prepare a litter for me and bring me to her." Then the servants carried him on a litter, and his son Rev and a great crowd of the people went with him.
When they came to Saint Nino's dwelling, they laid the queen on her haircloth, and Saint Nino began to pray to God and entreat Him
for a long time. Then she took the cross that she had and touched it to the queen's head, feet and shoulders in the shape of a cross. At once the queen was healed and rose up restored to life.
And she believed in Christ and said: "There is no other God but Christ, whom this captive woman preaches."

From then on she made Nino her close friend. She always questioned her and examined the faith of Christ in detail, and Saint Nino taught her, along with Abiathar, the new Paul, and his daughter Sidonia.
And the queen became a believer and came to know the true God. And the king asked the queen how she had been healed so suddenly.
And the queen told him everything that had happened to her: how she had been healed without medicine, through prayer and the touch of the cross.
And the crowd of people who had seen it confirmed the queen's words.

Then King Mirian was amazed and began to look into the faith of Christ. Many times he questioned Abiathar, who had been a Jew, about the Old and New Testaments, and Abiathar explained everything to him.
King Mirian also had a book of Nimrod, and in that book too he found this written: At the building of the tower there was a voice from heaven to Nimrod, which said to him:
"I am Michael, who am appointed by God over the dominion of the East. Go out from that city, for God is covering [i.e. overwhelming?] that city.
But in the last times the King of heaven, whom you desire to see, will come among a despised people.
Through fear of him the pleasures of the world will pass away; kings will abandon their kingship and seek poverty. He will look upon you in your distress and will save you."
Then King Mirian understood that the old books and the new bore witness, and that the book of Nimrod also confirmed it, and a desire for the law of Christ arose in him.
And the invisible enemy fought against him, holding him back from confessing Christ and casting into his heart hope in the idols and in fire. But
the queen continually entreated him to confess Christ. And from the queen's conversion the king remained for one year in double-mindedness.
Meanwhile holy Nino taught the people unceasingly, and she told no one "who I am or where I come from," but called herself a captive.
"After this the Magian, the Persian prince named Khuara, fell sick. He was severely tormented by an evil spirit and was near death, and that prince was of the kin of King Mirian.
Then Queen Nana and the king entreated holy Nino, but the king regarded her work with some double-mindedness.
He said to holy Nino: "By the power of which god do you perform this healing? Are you a daughter of Armazi, or a child of Zadeni,
who came as a stranger and fell down before them, and their mercy came upon you and they granted you the power of healing, so that by it you might make your living in a foreign land?
May they be glorified forever! As for you, be before us as one of the nurses of our children, and be honoured in this city.
But do not speak this strange word, the law of those erring Romans; do not even wish to speak of it at all.
For behold, the great gods, the rulers of the world, who spread the sunlight, who give the rain and nourish the offspring of the earth, the gods of Kartli,
Armazi and Zadeni, searchers of all that is hidden, the ancient gods of our fathers, Gatsi and Gaim: these have been worthy of men's trust.
Now if you heal this prince, I will make you rich and settle you as a resident of Mtskheta, as a servant of Armazi.
Although his shattering came upon him through that wind and hail, yet that place is invincible. This Armazi of the Georgians and the god of the Chaldeans,
Itrujan, are utter enemies: this one brought the sea against that one, and that one brought such affliction upon this one, as is the custom of the rulers of the world.
"And let this command of mine be enough for you." Blessed Nino answered:
"You, king: in the name of Christ, and through the prayers of his mother and of all the saints with him, may God, the Creator of heaven and earth, send down upon you,
may the Maker of every created thing send down upon you, out of his great and glorious and countless abundant mercy,
a single spark of his grace, like a spark from a furnace, so that you may know and understand the height of heaven and the light of the sun,
the depth of the sea and the breadth of the earth and its foundation. And may it be made known to you, king, who it is who clothes the heavens with cloud and thunders with the voice of the air,
and by whose might the earth shakes, and thunderbolts run, and fire blazes in his track because of his wrath.
Or when that great dragon stirs in the seas, the whole earth quakes, until the firm mountains, the cliffs and the rocks are shattered.
And I have made you understand all this, bringing you to it: that God is in the heavens, and he himself is invisible to all created beings, except his Son,
who came forth from him and appeared on earth as a man, who fulfilled everything for which he had come, and ascended to those same heights with the Father.
And he alone has seen the One without beginning, who is high and looks upon the lowly, and knows the lofty from afar.
O king, the time is near for you to draw close and look to God, for there is a sign in this city:
the robe of the Son of God is here, and some have said that the mantle of Elijah is here as well. And
there are many miracles that God has revealed.
And now I will heal this prince of yours by the power of Christ my God and by the cross of his passion, just as I healed the queen of a great illness.
And let him do what I have told him, so that he may enlighten his own soul and also bring his people near to God."
"And they brought the prince to her, and the queen also came into the garden, under the fir trees. And she set him facing east, [?] to raise his hands and to say three times:
'I renounce you, devil, and I follow Christ the Son of God.' And Nino wept, sighing from her soul.
And she asked God to help that man. And her disciples stayed right there for one day and two nights.
And quickly the evil spirit went out of him. And they became disciples of Nino, with their household and their people, and they glorified God."
The account of the woman Sidonia, who was a disciple of Nino, who saw and wrote down the conversion of King Mirian through a miracle,
and Nino's entreaty for the confession of Christ, for the raising of the cross, for the building of churches, and for the miracles in them.
Chapter Seven. Father, bless us. "And it happened one summer day, on the twentieth of the month of July, on a Saturday,
that the king went out hunting in the direction of Mukhnari, and the invisible enemy, the devil, came upon him and cast into his heart love for the idols and for fire.
And he thought about all their worship and about putting all the Christians to the sword. And the king said to his four counsellors:
"We deserve to have evil done to us by our gods, for we have become negligent in their service and have allowed the Christian
sorcerers to preach their faith in our land; for they perform those wonders by sorcery.
Now this is my plan: that we cruelly destroy all who believe in the Crucified One, and devote ourselves more fully to the worship of the gods who rule Kartli.
Let us urge Nana, my wife, to repent and abandon the faith of the Crucified One; and if she does not obey me, I will forget my love for her and destroy her too along with the others."
And those counsellors confirmed his plan, for they were ardent in this matter; they had wanted it from the beginning but had not dared to say so openly.
But the king went round all the surroundings of Mukhnari and climbed the high mountain of Tkhoti, so that he might look out toward Kaspi and Uplistsikhe.

He went up to the summit of the mountain. Exactly at midday the sun grew dark on the mountain, and it became like a dark, pitch-black night, and darkness took hold of the surrounding regions and places.
And they were scattered from one another in distress and anguish. And the king was left alone, and he wandered through the mountains and the tall forests, frightened and trembling.
He stood still in one place, and he had lost all hope of staying alive. And when he came back to his senses, he reasoned this way in his heart:
"Look at this: I called on my gods and found no relief for myself.
Now, the cross and the Crucified whom Nino preaches, through trust in whom she performs healing: would he not have the power to deliver me from this distress?
For I am in hell while still alive, and I do not know whether this ruin has come upon the whole earth, or whether it has come upon me alone.
Now, if this distress is for me alone, O God of Nino, light up this darkness for me and show me the way to my dwelling; and I will confess your name, and I will set up
the wood of the cross and worship it, and I will build a house of prayer for myself, and I will be obedient to Nino in the law of the Romans."
As soon as he had said all this, day broke and the sun shone forth. And the king dismounted from his horse, stood in that same place, stretched out his hands toward heaven, facing east, and said:
"You are God above all gods and Lord above all lords, the God of whom Nino speaks;
and your name is to be praised by all creation, under heaven and upon earth. For you have delivered me from distress and lit up my darkness.
Behold, I have come to know that you desire my salvation, my relief, and my drawing near to you, O blessed Lord.
In this place I will set up the wood of the cross, through which your name will be glorified and this miraculous deed will be remembered forever."
And he marked that place and set out. They saw the light, and the scattered people gathered together. And the king cried out:
"Give glory to Nino's God, for he is God from eternity, and to him alone glory is fitting forever."
And Queen Nana and all the people went out to meet the king.
For they had first heard that he was lost, and then that he was returning in peace, and they went to meet him at Kindzara and Gharta.
Now blessed Nino had stood for evening prayer in the bramble thicket, as was her custom at that hour, and with her were we, fifty souls.
And as the king arrived, the city was stirred up, and the king cried out in a loud voice:
"Where is that foreign woman, who is my mother, and whose God is my saviour?" And when they told him:
"She is here in the bramble thicket, praying," the king himself came with his whole army. The king got down from his horse and said to Nino:
"Now I am worthy to be called by the name of your God, my deliverer."
And holy Nino taught him and told him to worship at once toward the east and to confess Christ, the Son of God.
Then everyone wailed and wept when they saw the king and queen in tears.
And the next day King Mirian sent envoys to Greece, to Constantine, king of the Greeks, along with a letter from Nino to Queen Helena.
And they reported all these miracles of Christ that had been done in Mtskheta for King Mirian, and they urgently asked for priests to baptize the people.
Meanwhile holy Nino and her disciples preached to the people day and night without rest, and showed them the true way to the kingdom of heaven."
Her own account of the building of the church: "When the king and all the people had eagerly turned to Christianity, before the priests arrived, the king said to holy Nino:
'I am eager to build a house of God. Where should I build it?' Holy Nino said to him: 'Wherever the mind of kings is settled.' The king said to her:
"These brambles of yours are dear to me, and in my mind I wish for that place, but I will not do so;
instead I will not spare the royal garden, nor the height of these fir trees, nor the fruitfulness of these babilo trees [?], nor the fragrance of the flowers.
For the vision that you saw, of those birds with unsightly wings being washed in water and turning brilliantly white,
and of them perching on the trees of the garden and singing with sweet voices: truly, let this bodily, perishable garden be changed for us into an eternal paradise,
and let us build the house of God there as a place of prayer for us until the priests come from Greece.'
At once he set to work [?] and gave instructions to the carpenters. He cut down that fir, and from that fir they prepared the seven columns of the church.
When they had built the wall out of timber, they set up six of the columns, each in its own place.
But they could not raise the largest column. It was marvellous to look at and had been prepared to be set in the middle of the church.
They told the king about the marvel: the column could not be moved at all, not even from where it lay. "Then the king came with a crowd of people.
They brought machines of many kinds, and they tried to raise it by skill and by the strength of the crowd, but they could not.
The king and the crowd were astonished and said, 'What is this?' When evening came, the king went to his house, greatly troubled.
But holy Nino and her twelve women disciples stayed by the column.
And the blessed woman mourned over the column and shed tears.
Exactly at midnight, both of the mountains, Armazi and Zaden, seemed to topple over, as if they had collapsed and blocked the waters of both rivers.
The Mtkvari burst out and was sweeping the city away, and terrible sounds of wailing and lamentation arose.
In the same way the Aragvi came down on the fortress, and there was a terrible roaring. The women were afraid and began to flee.
But blessed Nino cried out: 'Do not be afraid, my sisters. The mountains are standing in their places, the waters are flowing in their places, and all the people are asleep.
The mountains seemed to collapse because this is a true sign shown to you: the mountains of unbelief have collapsed in Kartli.
The waters were blocked as a sign that the blood of children offered to the idols will be stopped.
And this sound of wailing comes from the crowd of demons, who are mourning for themselves because they are being driven out
of this place by the power of the Most High and by the cross of Christ. Turn back and pray to God.'
At once those voices died down, and there was nothing. Saint Nino stood with her hands spread out and prayed to God, saying:
"May this work that the king has undertaken not be hindered."
Then, before the cock had crowed, a mighty army struck terror at all three gates of the city:
the gates were broken down, and the city was filled with the Persian army. A terrifying noise arose: clamour, shouting and slaughter.
Every place was filled with blood. A multitude came with shouting and with swords, and the flesh of the others melted from fear, and their spirit failed.
They were weeping for their kinsfolk. "And suddenly a voice was heard as they shouted loudly:
'The king of the Persians, the king of kings Khuaran-Khuara, commands: Save all the Jews from the edge of the sword.'
When I heard this, I came to my senses. I and the ten who were with me wavered in our faith. The swordsmen had come close around us, striking and killing.
Then a loud voice was heard: "King Mirian has been captured!" The brave struggler looked around and said: "I know that this one who is crying out is now in great distress."
"I thank God, for this is the sign of their destruction, of the life of Kartli, and of the glory of this place."
And she comforted us like a skilled teacher, truly a teacher and apostle of Christ. She turned to the approaching people and said:
"Where are the kings of the Persians, Khuara and Khuaran-Khuara? You set out from Sabastan yesterday; you have certainly come quickly, and you are certainly a great army,
You have mightily broken down this city and put it to the sword. May winds and breezes carry you off into the darkness of the north, to the mountains and the cedars. Behold, the one has come
from whom you flee." She moved her hand in the sign of the cross, and at once all of them vanished.
A great stillness fell, and the women called her blessed and glorified God.
As dawn was breaking, all the women fell asleep. But I, Sidonia, stayed awake. And she stood with her hands spread out.
And behold, while this was so, a youth stood over the blessed one. He was adorned entirely with light and wrapped in a cloak of fire, and he spoke some three words to her.
She fell on her face. The youth put his hand to the pillar, raised it up, and carried it off into the height.
And in amazement I went up to her and said: 'Queen, what is this?' And she said to me:
"Bow your head to the ground," and in that terror he began to weep. After a short time he rose, raised me up, and we left that place.
The women, who were off at the edge, also saw the pillar. It came down in the likeness of fire and drew near to rest on its base, on the cut stump at the root of the fir tree.
When it was just the first glimmer of dawn, the king got up, disheartened by his sorrows. He looked toward the garden and the church that had been begun,
where his mind was fixed, and he saw a light like lightning reaching up to heaven from his garden.
He began to run and came quickly. The whole multitude of his household and all the people of the city came with him.
They saw the wonder: the pillar, shining with light, was coming down to its own place as if from heaven. It stood on the base and was set firm without being touched by human hands.
Blessed was he at that time, for as this was happening, the city of Mtskheta was filled with fear and joy, and rivers were flowing
…with tears, the kings, the princes and all the people. With longing in their souls they glorified God and called the blessed Nino blessed.
And great miracles took place on that day. First there came a certain Jew, blind from birth;
he came near to the pillar and received his sight on the spot, and he glorified God. Second, there came a royal child, a boy named Amazaspan; he was eight years old and lay sick.
His mother brought him in faith and laid him on a bed before the pillar of light, truly a pillar of light, and she pleaded with Nino:
"Look upon this son of mine, lady, for he is near death. For I know that the God whom you serve and preach to us is the God of gods."
Then the holy Nino touched the pillar with her hand, laid it on the boy and said:
"Believe in Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who came in the flesh for the life of the whole world. Be healed from now on, and glorify him by whose power you have been healed."
And at once the boy rose up as if he had never been in pain. And great fear fell upon the king and all the people.
And sick people of every kind kept coming and being healed, until the king built a wooden covering around the pillar and hid it from sight.
Even so, the people touched that covering and were healed. The king quickly began the church in the garden and completed it.
"And when King Mirian's envoys reached Constantine, king of the Greeks, they told him everything that had happened.
Then the king and his mother, Queen Helena, were filled with joy:
first, because the grace of God was spreading to every place, and all Kartli was being baptized under their hand;
and second, they rejoiced because they had received King Mirian's assurance that he had completely broken with the Persians and had firmly accepted their friendship.
And they glorified God and gave thanks to him. And he sent a true priest, John, as bishop, and with him two priests and three deacons. And King Constantine wrote Mirian
a letter of prayer and blessing and of thanksgiving to God.
And he sent a cross and an icon of the Saviour, and with them a great gift. And Queen Helena wrote a letter of praise and encouragement.
"Bishop John came to Mtskheta, and with him came the priests, the deacons and the envoys.
The king, the queen and all their people were filled with joy, because every one of them longed to be baptized.
Then King Mirian quickly sent an order to all the eristavis, the commanders and all the leading persons of the kingdom, summoning them before him. And they all quickly arrived in the city.
"Then the king was baptized at the hand of the holy Nino. After him the queen and their children were baptized at the hands of the priests and deacons.
After this they blessed the river Mtkvari. The bishop prepared a place near the gate of the bridge of Mogueti,
where the house of Elioz the priest had stood. There he baptized the nobles one by one, and that place was called the Baptistery of the Princes.
Below it, also on the riverbank, in two places, the two priests and the deacons baptized the people.
The people pushed against one another in their eagerness and begged the priests to baptize each of them first.
And so the people were eager for baptism, for they had heard the preaching of Saint Nino, who said:
"Everyone who is not baptized will not find the eternal light." And for this reason they were all quick to be baptized.
And in this way all the people and the multitude of Kartli were baptized, except only the mountaineers of the Caucasus, who were not baptized.
Nor did they come to that spreading of the light; instead they remained in darkness for some time.
And the Jews of Mtskheta were not baptized either, except that fifty households of the Barbians were baptized and became true Christians.
For this reason they became great before the king, and he granted them the village called Tsikhe-Didi.
But Peroz, the son-in-law of King Mirian, was not baptized. He held Ran as far as Barda, which King Mirian had given him.
Nor were his people baptized; they served King Mirian only in bodily matters.
Then King Mirian sent Bishop John, and with him a nobleman, to King Constantine,
and he asked for a portion of the Wood of Life, which the God-loving Queen Helena had discovered at that very time.
And he asked for many priests, so that he might send them to all the cities and places and they might baptize the people, so that every soul of Kartli might quickly be baptized.
And he asked for stonemasons to build churches. When they reached the Emperor Constantine,
he gladly bestowed a portion of the Wood of Life, and the boards on which the Lord's feet had been nailed, and the nails of the hands.
And he sent a great many priests and builders, for King Constantine, during his reign, built five hundred holy churches, temples of God.
He gave a great amount of treasure to Bishop John and commanded him:
"Wherever you think fit among the places of Kartli, build churches in my name, and endow the cities of Kartli with these gifts."
So the bishop set out, and the apostle with him. When they reached the place called Erusheti, he left builders there to work on the church.
He left treasure and the nails of the Lord, and went on. And he left builders at Tsunda
and treasure, and when the church had only just been begun, he went on and came to Manglisi, and began building a church; and he left there the boards of the Lord.
Then King Mirian was troubled by this, because they had not come first to the royal city, but had begun building churches in other cities and places and had left the relics there.
But Saint Nino came before the king and said: "Do not be troubled, O king, for this is how it should be: wherever they go, they sow the name of God.
And in this city is the glorious robe of the Lord."
Then the king summoned Abiathar the priest, and many Jews with him, and questioned them about the tunic.
And they told him everything that is written above. Then King Mirian raised his hands and said:
"Blessed are you, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, for from the very beginning you willed our deliverance from the devil and from that place of darkness.
Therefore you took your holy garment out of the holy city of Jerusalem from those Hebrews, who had become estranged from your divinity, and gave it to us, who are of foreign races."
"And the king and the whole city went forward steadfastly in Christianity, and the builders began to build the church outside the wall,
on the place of the bramble bushes, at the dwelling of Saint Nino, where the episcopal church now stands.
Then Saint Nino said: "Blessed is the Lord God Jesus Christ and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
who sent his holy Word from the highest heavens. He himself came down from the mighty throne to the earth in humility and was born,
without doubt, of the seed of David, born of a woman alone [?], holy and undefiled;
who was pleasing to him by reason [?], the cause of our life, who enlightened everything under heaven and saved those who believe;
who was born as a man, the light of all, the image of God the Father, and like some servant of the Law was baptized with water
and the Spirit. He was crucified, was buried and rose on the third day, and ascended on high to the Father, and he will come again in glory;
to whom belong all glory, honour and worship, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit."
On the Raising of the Venerable Cross. When the king and the queen and their children and all the people had been baptized,
there stood at that time a tree in a certain place, on a rock on an inaccessible hill. That tree was very beautiful and fragrant.
And this was the marvel of that tree: any wild animal struck by an arrow that came and ate its leaves or its seed would escape death, even if it had been badly wounded in a mortal spot.
This seemed very marvellous to those who had formerly been pagans, and they told Bishop John about the tree. And the bishop said:
"Behold, truly this land has been kept by God from the very beginning for his own service, for that tree sprang up from God and was preserved for this time.
For now the grace of God has been poured out over Kartli, and it is fitting to make from that tree a venerable cross, which the whole multitude of Kartli shall worship."
And Rev, the king's son, and the bishop and a multitude of people went out, and they cut down that tree and brought it away with its branches.
And ten times ten men carried it upright, with its branches and leaves, and brought it into the city.
And the people gathered to see how green it was and how full of leaves in wintertime, when every other tree was bare. But this one had not shed its leaves; it was fragrant and beautiful to look at.
And they set that tree up on its root at the door of the church, on the south side, where a gentle breeze blew and spread out the leaves of the tree and stirred its branches.
And its appearance was beautiful, as we know from hearsay, like that of the poplar tree [?]. They cut it down on the twenty-fifth of March, on a Friday.
And that tree stood thus for thirty-seven days, and its leaves did not change colour; it was just as when it stood on its own root
at the head of the spring. This lasted until all the trees of the forest were clothed with leaves and the fruit-bearing trees were clothed with blossom.
Then, on the first of the month of May, they made these crosses, and on the seventh of that month they raised them up by the laying on of hands of the kings,
with the joy and eagerness of all the people of the city, and they stood inside the church. All the people of the city saw, during all those days:
Behold, a cross of fire would come down from heaven, surrounded by something like a crown of stars, and it would stand over the church until dawn.
And just at daybreak two stars would come out of it: one would go eastward and one westward;
and the cross itself, still shining brightly, would move slowly out toward the Aragvi and stand on the rocky hill,
on the upper side, near the spring that the tears of Saint Nino had brought forth, and from there it would rise up to heaven.
And so all the people saw the saving power of our God many times.
Then they began to ask the blessed Nino: "What does it mean that a shining star comes out, and one goes eastward and one westward?"
And she said: "Send men onto the high mountains to the east
as far as the mountain of Kakheti, and to the west as far as the borders of this city; and when those stars shine out, let them watch
where they come to rest, and let these crosses of Christ be set up there too." Then the king did so, and the mountaintops were guarded continuously.
That day was Friday, and Saturday was dawning. The same miracle took place, and it happened just as it had happened before.
The next day the men from the west, who had been standing on the mountains of Kvabtatavi, came and told the king:
"That star came out, rose up and reached the mountain of Tkhoti, over the pass of Kaspi; it stopped at one spot and became completely invisible."
Likewise people came from the mountains of Kakheti and said: "We saw a star moving from here, and it stopped over the village of Bodi in Kukheti." Then the blessed Nino commanded:
"Take two crosses. Set up one at Tkhoti, where God revealed his power to me. Give the other to Salome, the handmaid of Christ, and let her set it up in the city of Ujarma."
For Bodi, a village of Kukheti, shall not take precedence over the city of the kings, because there is a multitude of people in it.
But the village of Bodi will itself later see that place pleasing to God." And they did just as the queen had commanded.
By this sign, a vision from heaven, they took up the precious cross in Mtskheta with human hands, and we went to the foot of that hill.
They spent the night at that spring and prayed to God, and the blessed Nino mingled her tears with the spring, and healings and great miracles took place.
The next day they went up onto that rock. And the blessed woman came onto that hill and fell down on the stones;
she wept, and with her the kings and the princes and all the multitude of the people, until the mountains echoed. And she laid
her hand on one stone and said to the bishop: "Come, for it is fitting for you to do so, and mark a cross on this stone." And he did so, and there the cross was set up by the kings with glory.
And the countless people bowed down and worshipped the cross, and confessed the Crucified One as truly the Son of the living God.
And they believed in God glorified in Trinity. The great princes did not leave the holy church,
the pillar of light, and the life-giving cross, because they saw those boundless miracles and those healings beyond telling.
And on the Lord's day (Sunday), the feast of the Fulfilment, King Mirian and all Mtskheta kept the feast,
and they offered the offering. They appointed that day for the service of the Cross, the feast of the Fulfilment, to be kept by all Kartli from that day to this day.
And some days afterward, after the [?] ("martvili", literally "martyr"), on a Wednesday, they saw a very great and awesome sign:
Behold, a pillar of light in the form of a cross stood over that cross, and twelve stars in the form of a crown were around it, and the hill smoked as if with fragrant incense.
And everyone saw this sign, and many of the godless were converted and were baptized on that day.
And the Christians became more faithful and glorified God.
Then they saw another sign of the Cross again: something like fire stood over its top, seven times brighter than the sun.
It rested upon it, and just as sparks rise from a furnace, so angels of God went up and came down upon it.
And the hill shook violently, and as the sign died down, so the shaking also died down.
When they saw that sign, everyone was amazed, and they glorified God more and more.
And as these signs took place year after year, all the people watched them with fear and trembling, and they came eagerly to worship.
At that time Rev, the king's son, had a small infant child, and it was sick and close to death.
Because he was their only child, she took him, laid him before the cross, and said in tears:
"If you grant me this child alive, I will build a shrine as a dwelling for you." At that very moment the child was healed, and she took him away healed and restored to life.
Then he came to fulfil his vow and gave thanks with great joy.
And Rev, the king's son, eagerly built the vault of the Cross of Mtskheta, and year after year he would come and fulfil that vow of sacrifice.
And from then on, even more of the weak and the sick came, were healed, and joyfully glorified the holy Cross of Christ.
There was a certain young man, and both of his eyes had gone blind.
He sat before the Cross of Christ, and after seven days his eyes were opened. He could see, and he glorified the venerable Cross.
Then there was a certain woman who was continually tormented by an evil spirit, to such a degree that it had taken away her strength and her mind for eight years, and she would tear her own clothing.
And when they brought her and made her touch the venerable Cross, after twelve days she was healed and went away on her own feet.
And she glorified God and worshipped the venerable Cross. And again, there was a certain little child who suddenly fell and died.
His mother picked him up and laid that dead child before the Cross, from morning until evening.
And his mother prayed before the Cross, weeping, and others said to her: "Woman, take him away and bury him, for he is dead, and do not trouble anyone any longer."
But she did not give up hope; instead she wept and prayed all the more pitifully. And at the hour of evening he came back to life, and his eyes opened.
And after seven days he was healed, and his mother took the boy away alive. And she glorified God.
When they saw the miracle and healing of the all-holy Cross, many who were childless came and asked for children. They became the parents of many children, and they made offerings and thanksgivings.
Not only did those who came receive healing, but also those who prayed to the holy Cross from far away
immediately received grace through its help. They overcame their enemies and quickly came to make thank-offerings.
So many godless people fell into distress, and when they called on the holy Cross,
they were immediately delivered from distress. They came to meet the precious Cross, were quickly baptized, and glorified the precious Cross.
So many who had fallen into much distress were healed of all kinds of torments by the power of the precious Cross.
They would hurry to pray and be healed at once, and so it is to this very day. And they glorified the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
The letter that the Patriarch of Rome and the King of the Franks wrote to Nino, to King Mirian, and to all the people of Kartli. In those days a letter came from Rome
from the holy Patriarch to Nino, to the king, and to all the people of Kartli. And he sent a Frankish deacon to offer praise and
to give a blessing, and to take away prayers from this blessed Nino and share in her grace.
He also had a letter from the King of the Franks for Nino, because the land of the Franks had been baptized through her father.
And all this had been heard of in Jerusalem and Constantinople: that the Sun of Righteousness had spread its light over the land of Kartli.
For this reason he wrote the blessed letter, so that he might learn about the miracles here: those of the pillar and of the bramble bush, and that power of healing.
The Frankish deacon saw all this and heard of the miracles that had taken place in Mtskheta, and in amazement he glorified God.
He took the letters and departed. Then the king said to holy Nino and to the bishop:
"I wish that we would convert the mountaineers and my son-in-law Peroz by force, with the sword, and make them servants of the Son of God and make them worship the precious Cross."
Then they said: "The Lord has not commanded us to take up the sword. Instead, let us show them the true way with the Gospel and the precious Cross,
the way that leads to eternal life, and let the grace of God enlighten the darkness of their hearts."
And holy Nino and Bishop John set out, and the king sent one of his eristavis (dukes) with them.
They went and stopped at Tsobeni, and called together the mountaineers, those men who were like beasts: the people of Chartali, the Pkhovians, the people of Tsilkani, and the people of Gudamakari.
And they preached to them the true faith of the Christians, which leads to eternal life. But they did not want to be baptized.
Then the king's eristavi turned the sword on them a little, and by force he smashed their idols.
They came down from there and stopped at Zhaleti, and preached to the people of Ertso and Tianeti.
And they accepted it and were baptized. But the Pkhovians left their land and crossed over into Tusheti.
And many others of the mountain people did not convert either, and when they would not accept baptism, the king made their tribute heavier.
